name: l1dump
title: firmware plaintext dumper (L1 SRAM out over USB / audio)
summary: Copies the decrypted on-chip memories (L1 instruction SRAM, L1 data A/B, scratchpad - plaintext only exists in the running chip, te-boot decrypts them while loading) into a CRC-framed static image (L1 instruction SRAM is read through the core's DTEST data-array interface: a normal load there faults) and sends it back to the Mac two ways: passively via USB disk mode (an after-hook on the usb_ms_yaffs sector read replaces blocks of a pre-placed carrier file; RAM only, nothing written to NAND) and audibly as an FSK stream on the audio out. Nothing runs at boot (a boot-time fault would hang the device before the UI): the first shift + speech captures and arms both paths; it also toggles the modem sound. Decode both with tools/l1dump_rx.py. Debug/preservation tool: the dumps are TE's firmware, keep them local (analysis/ is gitignored).

entry_hooks.what: usb_ms_yaffs.cpp sector read read(buf, sector, nsectors): after TE fills buf from the backing file, replace pre-placed carrier blocks (OP1DMPY1 + index + 0xA5 fill) with dump slices

controls: shift + speech: audio modem on / off (the USB carrier patching is always armed)
